newsitem.title: FRANCE: Former premier confirms Mitterrand hid cancer.
newsitem.headline: Former premier confirms Mitterrand hid cancer.

text.p: Late French President Francois Mitterrand's first prime minister said on Sunday the head of state had told him as early as 1981 about his cancer, a disease Mitterrand revealed only a decade later.

Socialist Pierre Mauroy, appointed premier when Mitterrand was elected to his first seven-year term in 1981, told Europe-1 radio in an interview: "Right at the beginning, he told me about his illness in confidence.

"As a result, I followed him. I know how he wanted to tackle his sickness, how he even succeeded, and with what joy he worked from the very beginning of his first seven-year term and with what courage he faced his illness," Mauroy added.
Mitterrand's personal doctor Claude Gubler revealed shortly after the former president's death a year ago that he misled voters for a decade by keeping his cancer secret.

Gubler's book "Le Grand Secret" (The Big Secret) was banned within 24 hours at the demand of Mitterrand's relatives, but newspapers widely reported that Mitterrand learned he had cancer within months of his first election in 1981 and kept it secret until 1992.

Rejecting the phrase "political lie", Mauroy, who is now mayor of Lille, said: "What chiefly remains is this courage on a human scale, the battle against disease and the fact that, even when you are sick, you can achieve very great things and have a vision of the future which is the vision of a changing world."
Gubler said in his book that Mitterrand's disease made him unfit to govern towards the end of his second term.
